pr_body:
It's possible to call `RecoveryTarget#restoreFileFromSnapshot` after the
`RecoveryTarget` has been replaced with a new instance due to a retry,
but before all its refs have been released. If the recovery was
snapshot-based then in this situation we will have already transferred
the permits to the new instance, so the assertion that this instance has
permits will trip. This commit fixes the problem with a non-null
placeholder value indicating that the recovery target was at least
originally created while holding some snapshot recovery permits.

Closes #96018

The underlying error seems to be [this one](https://gradle-enterprise.elastic.co/s/57brnuf4tdwpq/tests/:server:internalClusterTest/org.elasticsearch.snapshots.RestoreSnapshotIT/testChangeSettingsOnRestore/1/output):

```
	at java.base/java.util.concurrent.ThreadPoolExecutor$Worker.run(ThreadPoolExecutor.java:642)
	at java.base/java.lang.Thread.run(Thread.java:1623)
```

I have yet to understand why `assert hasPermitToDownloadSnapshotFiles();` fails in this scenario. I've been unable to reproduce it. It feels though like a genuine bug, since it should have the permit when it reaches that part of restoring from the snapshot.

One thing I see in the logs of the failure is that there were probably some relocations of shards that were cancelled because of a `cluster().wipeIndices("test-idx");` command of the test. That does not happen on every run. I would expect that the shards are gone for the command to return/complete. But I do wonder if there were any stale ongoing recoveries. I'll try to take more look into it, and if I cannot come up with something, I may continue with another test failure and hope the next person can delve more.
This seems super-rare but still an issue I think. The only failure in the last year was https://gradle-enterprise.elastic.co/s/ptwzzmbp6ecd4
